quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 RESULTS: ADJUSTED EPS AT THE TOP OF GUIDANCE, DATA-CENTER USAGE UP 17% FOR A SECOND YEAR. CFO David Poroch: adjusted earnings per share of $4.30 for 2025 was the very top of the 2025 guidance range and represents 6% growth (9% average annual growth from 2023). Weather-normalized total retail electricity sales rose 1.7% versus 2024, 'more than double the cumulative growth we saw over the last decade', with Georgia Power growing 2.5%. Commercial sales were 'led by increased usage from existing and new large load data center customers, which were up 17% year-over-year for the second year in a row'; industrial sales grew 1.4% and the company added 39,000 new residential electric customers. CEO Chris Womack: more than 120 companies located or expanded facilities in the electric and gas territories over the past year, supporting over 21,000 new jobs, and hyperscalers 'have made significant investments in our service territories.'
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS $4.30 for 2025 (6% growth); weather-normalized retail sales up 1.7%; Georgia Power 2.5%; data center customers up 17% year-over-year; industrial 1.4%; 39,000 new residential electric customers

quarterly_data.signal: CONTRACTED LARGE LOAD REACHES 10 GW ACROSS 26 PROJECTS; PIPELINE OVER 75 GW. Poroch: robust interest from large load customers, including hyperscalers, has materialized into 26 signed contracts representing 10 gigawatts of fully contracted electric service agreements, 2 gigawatts higher than last quarter and 4 gigawatts higher than a year ago. Nearly all of the 26 projects are under construction, with load ramps totaling 8 gigawatts by the end of the 5-year planning horizon and ultimately 10 gigawatts beyond 2030. The company is in late-stage discussions for another 10 gigawatts, 3 gigawatts of which are 'working through final reviews and are highly likely to progress to an executed contract in the near term'; Poroch confirmed the 2030 plan includes the 10 gigawatts signed plus these 3 gigawatts and nothing beyond. The total large load pipeline has increased to over 75 gigawatts as momentum grows in Alabama and Mississippi. On movement in the Georgia Power large load update, Poroch called it 'normal churn coming in and out of the pipeline' and said the short end of the pipeline 'has contracted a little bit' as counterparties, who also post collateral, refine their needs.
quarterly_data.figure: 26 signed contracts representing 10 gigawatts (2 gigawatts higher than what we reported last quarter and 4 gigawatts higher than a year ago); load ramps totaling 8 gigawatts by the end of the 5-year planning horizon; late-stage discussions for another 10 gigawatts, 3 gigawatts in final reviews; large load pipeline over 75 gigawatts

quarterly_data.signal: LONG-TERM SALES FORECAST RAISED TO 10% A YEAR ON LARGE-LOAD RAMPS. Poroch: retail electric sales across the three electric operating companies are projected to grow at least 3% in 2026, and annual electricity sales growth is projected to average 10% from 2026 through 2030, an increase of 2 percentage points from the prior long-term projection; Georgia Power's total retail electric sales growth is projected at approximately 13% over the same period. Based on the timing of load ramps in the risk-adjusted forecast, sales growth and the associated revenues are projected to accelerate into 2027 'with an even more pronounced expansion in 2028.' Commercial sales, roughly 1/3 of total retail sales, are projected to more than double, growing roughly 20% annually through the end of the decade.
quarterly_data.figure: retail electric sales growth of at least 3% in 2026; annual electricity sales growth of 10% on average from 2026 through 2030 (up 2 percentage points); Georgia Power approximately 13%; commercial sales growing roughly 20% annually

quarterly_data.signal: MULTI-YEAR EPS GUIDANCE INTRODUCED ON LARGE-LOAD GROWTH. Poroch: 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is $4.50 to $4.60 per share (7% growth from the 2025 guidance range), with a first-quarter adjusted EPS estimate of $1.20. The company expects to grow adjusted EPS 8% to 9% from 2026 through 2028 and set initial ranges of $4.85 to $4.95 for 2027 (approximately 8% growth) and $5.25 and $5.45 for 2028 (approximately 9% growth), with approximately 7% to 8% growth longer term from the 2028 range - an average of 8% from the 2026 guidance midpoint to 2030. The outlook is 'supported by a large and growing portfolio of large load contracts'; Poroch said management would be 'pretty disappointed if we didn't achieve near the top end' and sees upside from repricing Southern Power capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adjusted EPS guidance $4.50 to $4.60; Q1 estimate $1.20; 2027 initial range $4.85 to $4.95; 2028 initial range $5.25 and $5.45; 8% to 9% EPS growth from 2026 through 2028; 7% to 8% longer term

quarterly_data.signal: CAPITAL PLAN RAISED TO $81 BILLION, DRIVEN BY NEW GENERATION FOR LARGE LOAD. Poroch: the base capital investment forecast is $81 billion over the next 5 years, 95% of it at the state-regulated utilities, an $18 billion or approximately 30% increase from a year ago, driven mainly by new generation facilities (most announced or approved in 2025) and the approved Georgia IRP (uprates at existing natural gas and nuclear facilities, hydroelectric dam modernization). Roughly $42 billion through 2030 goes to serving projected growth through new generation, enhancements to existing generation and expansions of transmission and interstate pipeline systems, supporting state-regulated rate base growth of approximately 9%. The plan carries no capital placeholders; Alabama Power and Georgia Power RFPs for generation needed in the early to mid-2030s 'could represent several gigawatts of additional new generation', and Poroch gave a rough rule of thumb of $2 billion for a gig of incremental generation. Poroch noted Georgia Power 'just closed in December on 10 gigawatts' and said incremental capital above the plan would be financed with approximately 40% equity or equity equivalents.
quarterly_data.figure: base capital investment forecast $81 billion over the next 5 years, 95% at state-regulated utilities; $18 billion or approximately 30% increase; roughly $42 billion to serve projected growth; rate base growth of approximately 9%; $2 billion for a gig of incremental generation

quarterly_data.signal: LARGE-LOAD CONTRACT TERMS: 15-YEAR MINIMUMS, TAKE-OR-PAY-STYLE MINIMUM BILLS, COLLATERAL. Poroch: all three electric jurisdictions allow bilaterally negotiated large-load contracts rather than a standard tariff. Data-center contracts carry minimum terms of at least 15 years, fixed or minimum bill provisions 'similar to take-or-pay structures' designed to cover at least 100% of the annual incremental cost to serve (generation and transmission investment, incremental O&M and cost of capital), and termination payments backed by significant collateral requirements. As part of its December certification process for new generation, Georgia Power quantified at least approximately $1.7 billion of benefits lowering the cost to serve existing customers from 2029 through 2031, 'directly attributable to the value created by our approach to contracting'. Load taken beyond the minimum is priced at roughly the marginal cost and is upside to the plan.
quarterly_data.figure: minimum terms of at least 15 years; minimum bills to cover at least 100% of the annual incremental cost to serve; at least approximately $1.7 billion of benefits from 2029 through 2031

quarterly_data.signal: SOUTHERN POWER: GAS FLEET REPRICING AND UPRATES AS UPSIDE OUTSIDE THE PLAN. Womack: Southern Power has over 13 gigawatts of capacity across 55 generating facilities in 15 states, including over 7 gigawatts of natural gas generation in the Southeast, substantially all under long-term contracts. As gas-fleet contracts come up for renewal from the early 2030s, 'The market demand for capacity has increased pricing roughly 2 to 3x higher than where many of these assets are currently contracted', and by 2030 approximately 1,000 megawatts can be remarketed; Poroch cited market examples of 'around $20, maybe $25 a kilowatt month.' The company is in late-stage discussions on uprates of up to an additional 700 megawatts (as soon as '29 per Womack, not included in the plan) and is evaluating 6 brownfield sites in the Southeast for potential new gas development, always under long-term contracts with creditworthy counterparties. Asked whether the uprate capacity would be contracted with co-ops and other power companies rather than sold directly to data centers, Poroch said 'that's a very safe bet.'
quarterly_data.figure: over 13 gigawatts across 55 generating facilities; approximately 1,000 megawatts to remarket by 2030; uprates of up to an additional 700 megawatts; recontracting examples around $20, maybe $25 a kilowatt month (2 to 3x current contracts); 6 brownfield sites under evaluation

quarterly_data.signal: EQUIPMENT, LABOR AND FUEL FOR THE BUILDOUT SECURED IN ADVANCE. Womack: 'We secured the labor and equipment for these projects through early EPC agreements and reservation payments well in advance and are leveraging relationships across our vast supply chain', citing lessons from completing Plant Vogtle Units 3 and 4, 'the only 2 new nuclear units in 3 decades.' Asked about the status of gas supply and battery components for the '28 and '29 generation projects, Womack said 'It's all secured' and, pressed on whether that was physical or only financial, 'It is physically secured.'

BRIDGE POWER, GAS AND FIBER AS ADDITIONAL DATA-CENTER OPPORTUNITIES. Womack: the four gas LDCs 'operate in 3 of the top data center markets in the country and are active in discussions with several large customers on solutions to directly or indirectly serve this potential growth.' PowerSecure provides utility and energy solutions including bridge power and is positioned to grow as demand for customer-sided solutions increases; asked about demand, Womack said 'in the near term, there will be continued opportunities for bridge solutions in the market' and later called bridge solutions at Southern Power and PowerSecure 'potential upsides to the plan.' Southern Telecom deploys fiber optic infrastructure with the electric utilities, enhancing the appeal to data-intensive customers locating in the Southeast. Potential natural gas pipeline investments (FERC-regulated interstate pipelines or midstream-like LDC investments) to serve growing energy needs are also outside the base capital plan.
quarterly_data.figure: gas LDCs operate in 3 of the top data center markets
